candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall establish and enforce specific limits to implement the provisions of 40 CFR Parts 403.5(a) and (b), as required by 40 CFR Part 403.5(c).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether these 403.5-based limits are operative local/pretreatment limits for the facility during FY2025 affects which enforceable prohibitions or limits (Purpose A) must be identified and whether associated monitoring or enforcement obligations (Purpose B) apply.

candidates.exact_span: Such BMPs shall be considered local limits and Pretreatment Standards.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classifying BMPs as local limits and Pretreatment Standards versus non-limit management practices changes whether they are enforceable numeric or prohibition-style limits for compliance comparison (Purpose A) rather than report-only or non-comparable guidance.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall, within sixty (60) days of the effective date of this permit, (1) submit a WRITTEN CERTIFICATION that a technical evaluation has been demonstrated that the existing technically based local limits (TBLL) are based on current state water quality standards and are adequate to prevent pass through of pollutants, inhibition of or interference with the treatment facility, worker health and safety problems, and sludge contamination, OR (2) submit a WRITTEN NOTIFICATION that a technical evaluation revising the current TBLL and a draft sewer use ordinance which incorporates such revisions will be submitted within 12 months of the effective date of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which certification/notification path applies, and whether existing TBLL are deemed adequate versus under revision, affects which local limits are in force during FY2025 (Purpose A), whether related monitoring or program obligations are triggered (Purpose B), and whether missing or interim evidence should be treated as unresolved limit applicability versus a documented transitional state (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: All specific prohibitions or limits developed under this requirement are deemed to be conditions of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a prohibition or limit counts as a permit condition determines if it is an enforceable limit subject to numeric or prohibition-based compliance comparison rather than non-operative background text.

candidates.exact_span: The specific prohibitions set out in 40 CFR Part 403.5(b) shall be enforced by the permittee unless modified under this provision.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether 403.5(b) prohibitions remain in effect or have been modified under this provision changes which enforceable limits apply (Purpose A) and whether associated enforcement or monitoring tied to those prohibitions is required (Purpose B).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall analyze the treatment facility influent and effluent for the presence of the toxic pollutants listed in 40 CFR 122 Appendix D (NPDES Application Testing Requirements) Table II at least once/year and the toxic pollutants in Table III at least once/3 months.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mandated pollutants, media (influent and effluent), and minimum frequencies establish baseline monitoring obligations for FY2025 (Purpose B); absent reported results, whether monitoring was required on each schedule affects missing-evidence classification (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: If, based upon information available to the permittee, there is reason to suspect the presence of any toxic or hazardous pollutant listed in Table V, or any other pollutant, known or suspected to adversely affect treatment plant operation, receiving water quality, or solids disposal procedures, analysis for those pollutants shall be performed at least once/3 months on both the influent and the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability hinges on whether suspicion is established from available information, so different readings change whether quarterly influent/effluent analysis is required at all (Purpose B) versus conditional monitoring not being triggered (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The influent and effluent samples collected shall be composite samples consisting of at least 12 aliquots collected at approximately equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period and composited according to flow.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Composite design requirements define what sampling satisfies the monitoring obligation (Purpose B) and whether available sample evidence is adequate when fewer aliquots, a non-24-hour period, or non-flow weighting is used (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: Sampling and analytical procedures shall be in accordance with guidelines established in 40 CFR 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation of 40 CFR 136 methods and procedures affects whether reported monitoring meets permit-required methodology (Purpose B) and whether missing or nonconforming data leaves compliance or adequacy unresolved (Purpose C).

candidates.exact_span: The effluent samples shall be analyzed to a level at least as low as required in (6) below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required analytical quantitation level, as defined by the cross-referenced paragraph (6), affects whether effluent results can be compared to applicable numeric limits (Purpose A) and whether monitoring was performed to the required detection/reporting level (Purpose B).

candidates.exact_span: Where composite samples are inappropriate, due to sampling, holding time, or analytical constraints, at least 4 grab samples, taken at equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period, shall be taken.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether composite sampling is inappropriate determines if the obligation shifts to four grab samples instead, changing applicable monitoring design (Purpose B) and whether submitted data from a single grab or non-equal intervals counts as adequate evidence (Purpose C).
